children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--As expected, Intercontinental Exchange canola futures shed their losses to turn positive on Thursday. Earlier strong gains in crude oil spurred the Canadian oilseed's turnaround, but crude was now mixed.
Support for canola also came from increases in Chicago soybeans and soymeal, but soyoil remained weaker. There were also declines in most European rapeseed contracts and in Malaysian palm oil.

A measure of uncertainty continued in the canola market over its harvest. While Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada projected canola production at 21.6 million tonnes, varied crop conditions across the Prairies could result in reduced yields. Statistics Canada is set to issue its production report on Sept. 16.
The Saskatchewan crop report placed its canola harvest at four per cent complete and yields averaging 38 bushels per acre. The combining of all crops provincewide at 18 per cent done.
The Canadian dollar was climbing higher on Thursday afternoon, with the loonie reaching 72.53 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 72.13.
There were 50,674 canola contracts traded on Thursday, compared to 68,404 on Wednesday. Spreading accounted for 28,484 contracts traded.
